X-06 Customer registration

Bangla name: গ্রাহক নিবন্ধন

← 60 · Cross-cutting · Contents · Open queries

1. Name and purpose

Customer registration. A new customer creates a GoBCB account on the web portal or in the app. The account is a user in the User Cognito pool, created by the external identity API after the customer has proved both the email address and the phone number with one-time codes. A customer can also register with OneID instead, which happens on OneID's own site.

None of the five repositories contains the identity API; the clients' calls are the only evidence of how it behaves [UNCONFIRMED: Q-01].

2. Trigger and actor

Item Value
Actor Anonymous visitor
Client and screen Portal /:lang/auth/register → verify-email → email-verified → verify-phone → phone-verified → set-password. App: signup → emailOTP → emailVerification → phoneNumberOtp → phoneNumberVerification → setPassword (RoutePath in lib/presentation/navigation/route_path.dart)
Cognito pool User (account created by the identity API)
Role / program scope none

3. Business flow

  1. The customer enters name, email and 10-digit phone (the client adds +880) and accepts the terms.
  2. The platform stores the data provisionally and emails a code. The customer enters it ("email verified").
  3. The platform sends a code by SMS. The customer enters it ("phone verified").
  4. The customer chooses a password. The account is created; the portal opens the login page with a success message.
  5. OneID alternative (portal): "Register with OneID" opens OneID's registration page in a popup; when OneID redirects back to /:lang/auth/login, the popup closes and the customer logs in with OneID (X-08). The account in GoBCB is created at first OneID login.

4. Technical flow

All calls go to the identity API base URL (environment.services.identity in the portal, AUTH_API_BASE_URL in the app) with a static header Authorization: <environment.headerkey | AUTH_API_TOKEN>. No GoBCB backend service is involved.

# From → To Hop Request body (as sent by the client) On success
1 Client → identity POST user/register-cached [HTTP, static key] Portal: { name, email (lower-case), phone, dob: "1900-01-01", address: "n/a", verification_type: "mobile", verification_id: "0123456789" }. App: { name, email, phone, address, verification_type, verification_id, dob } Portal stores the payload as rvl_init_register and starts step 2
2 Client → identity POST otp/send-otp [HTTP, static key] { type: "email", destination: <email> } Navigate to verify-email
3 Client → identity POST otp/verify-otp [HTTP, static key] { type: "email", destination, otp } Navigate to email-verified
4 Client → identity POST otp/send-otp [HTTP, static key] { type: "sms", destination: <phone> } Navigate to verify-phone
5 Client → identity POST otp/verify-otp [HTTP, static key] { type: "sms", destination, otp } Response user_id stored as rvl_init_id
6 Client → identity POST user/register [HTTP, static key] Portal: { user_id, password }. App: { user_id, ekyc, address, password } Portal clears the stored values and opens /auth/login
7 identity API → Cognito User pool (outside the repos) — User created [UNCONFIRMED: Q-01]

Error codes the clients recognise (from status_message / exception text): user_already_exists, passport_or_nid_required (register-cached); user_not_found, user_data_incomplete, error_getting_verification_information, error_creating_user, error_saving_data_to_db, server_error (register).

6. API contracts

Method Path (identity API) Auth Request Response Main errors
POST user/register-cached static header key see step 1 not read by the portal user_already_exists, passport_or_nid_required
POST otp/send-otp static header key SendOtp { type, destination } not read status_message text
POST otp/verify-otp static header key VerifyOtp { type, destination, otp } { user_id } (phone step) invalid_otp (see X-09)
POST user/register static header key SignUpPayload { user_id, password } (portal) not read list in §4

Payload classes: rvl-gobcb-user-portal/ETP-Web/src/app/modules/core/models/user-auth.ts. OtpType values: sms, email (modules/core/enums/Enums.ts:15-18).

// POST {identity}/user/register-cached   (portal)
{
  "name": "Rahim Uddin",
  "phone": "+8801711111111",
  "email": "rahim@example.com",
  "dob": "1900-01-01",
  "address": "n/a",
  "verification_type": "mobile",
  "verification_id": "0123456789"
}

// POST {identity}/otp/verify-otp   (phone step)
{ "type": "sms", "destination": "+8801711111111", "otp": "482913" }

// 200 (only the field the portal reads)
{ "user_id": "<id issued by the identity API>" }

7. Data and side effects

  • Identity API: provisional registration, OTPs (email and SMS), finally the Cognito user. Where it stores the provisional data and the profile is not visible [UNCONFIRMED: Q-01].
  • Browser (portal) local storage: rvl_init_register, rvl_init_id, email_resend_code_timestamp, phone_resend_code_timestamp; removed after success.
  • No GoBCB table is written.

9. Handover notes

  1. The identity API is a black box. Registration, OTPs, profiles, password reset and app versions all live there and the source is in none of the repos [UNCONFIRMED: Q-01]. Ask BS23 for its repository, hosting and owner before go-live.
  2. The static key is shipped to clients. environment.headerkey (portal bundle) and AUTH_API_TOKEN (app .env, also printed by Logger.debug at app start, lib/main/main.dart:55) are readable by anyone with the client.
  3. The portal sends placeholder identity data (dob: "1900-01-01", address: "n/a", verification_id: "0123456789"). The app sends the real values and an ekyc field. Whether the identity API needs real NID/passport data is unclear: the app handles a passport_or_nid_required error [UNCONFIRMED: Q-01].
  4. App register hides unknown errors. AuthApiServiceImpl.register catches BaseException and rethrows only the six known messages; any other error message is swallowed and the flow continues as if it succeeded.
  5. The client trusts user_id from the OTP response and sends it back with the password. Whether the identity API ties user/register to a verified OTP server-side cannot be seen here.

11. Developer test guide

Local testability: Not locally. The identity API has no source; the user-portal proxy answers 503 for everything under /p/identity except a user/my-profile stub (docs/user-portal-local.md §5), and the mobile gateway answers 503 for /identity (docs/mobile-local.md §5). Use the seeded customer +8801700000011 / Passw0rd!23 instead of registering.

Item Detail
Test data and accounts Seeded User-pool customer +8801700000011 (floci/seed-users.ps1); create more with aws cognito-idp admin-create-user against Floci if needed
Browser http://localhost:4201/en/auth/register renders; submitting shows the 503 error. DevTools → Network shows POST /p/identity/user/register-cached with Authorization: <headerkey> (no Bearer)
Emulator pwsh ./scripts/Setup-MobileApps.ps1 -App user -Run; the sign-up screens open, calls to http://localhost:5200/identity/... return 503
Postman No collection covers the identity API
Visual Studio debug Not applicable (no GoBCB service involved)
Verify On a deployed environment: the new phone number appears in the User pool (aws cognito-idp list-users --user-pool-id <UserPoolId> --filter "phone_number = \"+880…\"")
